summary: Forest Service fire lookout at 6,070 ft on South Fork Mountain; a 1933 lookout on the site was destroyed in 1986 and a 1960 metal tower was moved in by helicopter.

facts.design: CL 160 cab with catwalk on a 19-foot tower

access.note: Staffed by Forest Service personnel in fire season and in active service. A 2023 hiker found the gates locked and stayed on the ground. No closure is stated in the sources read. Provisional: rests on one blog account and the register's visit note.

visit.trail_note: A 2023 hiker went up Horse Ridge Road (3S12) to a camp area and walked a little over four miles, partly along a Jeep trail. Do not climb; the cab is manned in fire season and was locked.

events.note: Earlier lookout on Horse Ridge, per the register visit note and Peakbagging. Destroyed in March 1986.
A family was on leave from the Horse Ridge lookout (Blue Lake Advocate item, as transcribed by Forest Lookouts).
George Russell, a veteran Forest Service lookout man, was posted at the station (Ukiah Daily Journal item, as transcribed).
Metal tower first built on Eight Mile in the Mad River District.
Earlier structure on Horse Ridge destroyed in March 1986.
Moved to Horse Ridge in June 1986 by National Guard helicopter. Peakbagging suspects the tower was rebuilt that year.
Date registered per the Register: January 2, 2006.
Register visit report, November 4, 2013: staffed by full-time Forest Service personnel in fire season.

corrections.why: The Register gives the tower as 19 feet (about 5.8 m). The record's 4.3 m is about 14 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1960 date in the record is for the metal tower built on Eight Mile. The Horse Ridge site had a lookout built in 1933, destroyed in March 1986.

notes_for_editor: Register number conflict: the NHLR detail page gives US 647, CA 77 for Horse Ridge, which matches the record's registers field. The FFLA California list (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) gives Horse Ridge NHLR US 1345, CA 168, lists the kind as 2-StoryCab, misspells the county as Trinty, and gives US 647 to Hot Springs Mountain. Moved versus rebuilt in 1986 is unresolved: the Register says moved, Peakbagging suspects a rebuild. The 1931 Shasta Courier item about 'Horse mountain near Bully Hill' concerns a different lookout and is left out. The 1961 cabin description is inferred to be the 1933 structure. Staffing as_of is the 2013 visit report; a current check would help. Access is a judgment call: manned, gates locked, no closure stated.
